newsDocuments.headline: Oil hits USD116 mark as ME conflict rages on

segments.text: NEW YORK: Oil prices settled more than USD3 higher on Friday, their highest in nearly six months after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concerns over further disruption to energy supplies from the Middle East, where UAE authorities als
Brent crude futures settled at USD116.72 a barrel, up USD3.55 or 3.14 percent, their highest since April 29. US West Texas Intermediate crude closed at USD103.27 a barrel, up USD3.80 or 3.8 percent.

“Fears of supply disruptions drove the advance after Houthi carried out a series of attacks across Saudi Arabia, including on energy infrastructure,” said Adam Turnquist, chief cross-asset strategist for LPL Financial.

newsDocuments.headline: UAE reports oil spill from tanker

segments.text: DUBAI: The United Arab Emirates reported an oil spill from a tanker off its coast on Friday, as numerous vessels in Gulf waters come under attack during the Middle East war.
Frequent attacks on ships have been reported in recent weeks near the Strait of Hormuz, at the heart of the conflict between Iran and the United States.
The authorities “detected a tanker oil spill affecting Umm Al Quwain’s beaches”, the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment said in a statement, referring to an emirate north of Dubai.

newsDocuments.headline: US authorises emergency release of up to 400,000 oil barrels

segments.text: WASHINGTON: The US Department of Energy said on Friday it had authorised an emergency exchange of up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address a supply disruption affecting Phillips 66’s Lake Charles re
The Lake Charles refinery has a capacity to refine about 264,000 barrels per day.

The exchange will “help offset temporary disruptions affecting crude oil deliveries to the refinery and support continued production of transportation fuels serving Louisiana and surrounding markets,” the department said.

newsDocuments.headline: European stocks down as oil prices dent earnings optimism

segments.text: FRANKFURT: European stocks suffered their steepest weekly loss since early September, as tensions in France and higher oil prices dampened the optimism sparked by some strong corporate earnings.
Overall earnings estimates have improved for European companies, but higher crude prices and the unrest in France have left investors jittery.

newsDocuments.headline: Govt raises diesel price by Rs1.91 per litre, keeps petrol unchanged

segments.text: The government has increased the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.91 per litre while keeping petrol price unchanged, effective for the next three days.

According to a press release issued by the Petroleum Division on Friday, the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA) revised the ex-depot prices of petroleum products under the federal government’s petroleum pricing mechanism.
The government on Thursday increased the price of high-speed diesel by Rs1.64 per litre and reduced petrol price by Rs1.60 per litre.
